source.title: Uncovering Branch Specialization in InceptionV1 Using K Sparse Autoencoders

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; it has minor OCR and typesetting errors.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses k-sparse autoencoders to analyze InceptionV1 features, motivated in part by superposition, but investigates branch specialization rather than testing the listed claims about superposition or its geometry.
record.gate_note: The reported results concern branch specialization and SAE-feature localization in InceptionV1. They do not test the listed versions: there is no toy-network capacity or sparsity experiment, LLM test, test of SAE-feature completeness or stability, or comparison of one-dimensional and multidimensional features. The paper’s general claims and cited findings are not recorded as results; the branch-localization findings below are relevant to the claim’s subject but fit no listed version.
record.test_reason: The study uses tied-weight k-sparse autoencoders as a tool on InceptionV1 (a vision CNN) to map branch specialization. It reports no toy-model experiments, no tests of capacity or other causes of polysemanticity, no LLM results, no checks of SAE-feature completeness or stability, and no feature-dimensionality comparison. Superposition is only invoked as motivation, so the paper bears on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also frame the results as showing features forming progressively across layers (from posed animals, to animal parts, to specific species). They describe the cross-layer patterns as examples of 'cross layer superposition', though they offer no test of superposition itself.
record.recipe_differences: The paper applies tied-weight k-sparse autoencoders with a latent expansion factor of 16 and k=32 to InceptionV1 activation vectors; it does not reproduce the toy-network experiments or method of Toy Models of Superposition.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE features trained on whole InceptionV1 mixed4 layers draw much of their decoder norm from particular convolution branches: animal features from 5x5 branches, colour features from a 1x1 branch. Similar specializations appear to recur across layers, shown by a circuit and by UMAP projections.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In InceptionV1, SAE features localize preferentially to specific convolution branches, and the branch specialization is consistent across adjacent layers.

record.peer_reviewed: 2025 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
record.problems: The paper says it provides examples rather than a full taxonomy. The reported branch specialization is largely qualitative, with no stated controls or uncertainty estimates; the UMAP comparison is qualitative. Branch-contribution findings do not test the listed superposition versions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were left out.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy networks, sparsity sweep, phase transition or geometry analysis.
All of it: no test of capacity, feature importance, or dedicated versus shared dimensions.
All of it: no test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
All of it: no LLMs are studied, and SAE recovery in a CNN is used, not evaluated.
All of it: no completeness, stability or canonicality tests of SAE features.
All of it: no comparison of 1-D and multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Single-author workshop paper with qualitative evidence: example features, figure captions, one circuit, and UMAP plots. It reports no controls and no uncertainty. The 'superposition' language is motivational only, so no verdict labels are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network experiment on feature count, sparsity, overlap, transition, or geometry.
No test of capacity pressure, feature importance, or dedicated versus shared dimensions as causes of polysemanticity.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
The study analyzes InceptionV1, not LLMs, and does not test the specified LLM evidence.
The study uses SAE features for analysis but does not test whether they are complete, stable, or canonical model units.
No comparison of one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Used SAE feature visualizations and examples to characterize specialization in the mixed4a 5x5 branch.
rows.value: The authors report that the mixed4a 5x5 branch specializes in complex geometric shapes.
rows.note: This is a branch-specialization result, not a test of a listed version.
rows.check: The 'feature type' condition is listed as not stated, but the text names complex geometric shapes, confirming a hypothesis from the Branch Specialization paper. The row is a qualitative branch-specialization result, not a superposition measure.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Used SAE feature visualizations and examples to characterize specialization in the mixed4b 5x5 branch.
rows.value: The authors report features for animals in specific orientations and poses, including animals facing or positioned left or right.
rows.note: The paper presents these as examples of branch specialization.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Used SAE feature visualizations and examples to characterize specialization in the mixed4c 5x5 branch.

conditions.value: animal orientations, poses, and general animal features

rows.value: The authors describe a mixture of orientation/pose features and more general animal features.
rows.note: The paper also reports that the mixed4c and mixed4b 5x5 branches appear to have similar specialization.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Used SAE feature visualizations and examples to characterize specialization in the mixed4d 5x5 branch.
rows.measure: Proportion of feature norm attributed to branch neurons
rows.value: Animal-part features are described as generally in the 0.4–0.6 range, with a majority represented by 5x5-branch neurons.
rows.note: The range and majority characterization are stated in the figure caption.
rows.check: The value is read from the Figure 6 caption only. The 0.4–0.6 range is a qualitative caption reading with no baseline. It is not linked to any version.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Measured SAE-feature contribution from neurons in the mixed4d 1x1 branch.
rows.measure: Proportion of learned feature represented by branch neurons
rows.value: Color features are described as generally represented to a large extent by neurons in the 1x1 branch.
rows.note: No numerical proportion is stated in the caption.
rows.check: There is no numeric value; it is a caption-level qualitative statement. The abstract also claims a mixed4a 1x1 result, but no figure for it is shown.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed feature and activation-vector relationships along a cross-layer circuit.
rows.measure: Branch contribution to a circuit feature
rows.value: A mixed4c animal feature is described as having about 40% of its total norm in neurons from the 5x5 branch.
rows.note: The authors also describe subsequent features associated with dog fur and lower body parts.
rows.check: The paper describes the ~40%-norm mixed4c feature inconsistently: the Figure 2 caption calls it an animal-face detector, while Section 3.2 says it detects animals near the bottom of the image. The row should note this. It is also a branch-localization measure, not a superposition measure.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Compared two-dimensional UMAP projections of SAE decoder vectors.
rows.value: The authors report similar rings or manifolds around other features in both projections, with more apparent clustering near the top in mixed4c than in the more uniform mixed4b projection.
rows.note: This is a qualitative projection comparison, not a test of feature dimensionality or canonical status.
rows.check: This is a qualitative UMAP comparison of decoder vectors. It does not test V5 or V6; the 'manifold' wording is about projection layout, not multi-dimensional features.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
